## 1. Introduction

Introduction: Introduce the context of your dataset and describe its source(s). Include hyperlink(s) for where you retrieved it from as well as a picture (with citation) related to your topic. Why did you pick this dataset to analyze, and what will you be investigating?

My first dataset provides health information on each US county and my second dataset is a table that I plan to web scrape a table that provides information on the number of those in poverty for each US county. I got the first data set from an organization called [County Health Rankings](https://www.countyhealthrankings.org/health-data/methodology-and-sources/data-documentation/national-data-documentation-2010-2023) and the second dataset comes from the [USDA government website](https://data.ers.usda.gov/reports.aspx?ID=4040). I picked these datasets so that I could explore the different factors around health. I will be investigating the relationship between variables such as obesity, low birthweight rates, poverty, smoking habits in each county, average amount of days spent in poor mental health, and percent of residents in poor health.

![](usa_health.jpg)

## Data Preparation

I obtained my first dataset through a website where I was able to easily download it. However, when I tried to import it, I realized it wasn't a csv file so I went on a website to convert the file. Then, when I tried to import it, the data got messed up so what I ended up doing was going into the Excel file and copying the table into google sheets so that I could then export that into a .csv file. I created 2 new variables because I needed to create categorical variables. I calculated the median of percentage of smokers across all counties and depending on if the value for a county was higher or lower, it would either be a "heavy smoker" county or a "light smoker" county. I did the same thing with obesity rates. For my second dataset, I tried to use html to easily web scrape it but I couldn't get it to work so I manually scraped it into a Google Sheets and then imported it to R. Then. I joined the 2 datasets. Also, when joining the datasets there was a duplicate of each row which was inflating the data so I used join <-distinct(join) in order to make sure each row was unique. After the dataset was joined, I realized that there were some rows that randomly had a missing value in the county column so I got rid of that. There are 3041 observations.

```{r}
US_COUNTY_HEALTH <- read.csv("US_COUNTY_HEALTH.csv")
Poverty <- read.csv("Poverty.csv")

library(tidyverse)

county_health <- data.frame()

for (i in 1:nrow(US_COUNTY_HEALTH)) {
  if (!any(is.na(US_COUNTY_HEALTH[i, ]))) 
    {
    county_health <- rbind(county_health, US_COUNTY_HEALTH[i, ])
  }
}

median(county_health$perc_smokers)
median(county_health$obesity)
  county_health<- as_tibble(county_health) |>
    rename(perc_smokers = `X..Adults.Reporting.Currently.Smoking`, low_birth = `X..Low.Birthweight`, obesity = `X..Adults.with.Obesity`, poor_health = `X..Fair.or.Poor.Health`, poor_mental = `Average.Number.of.Mentally.Unhealthy.Days`) |>
  mutate(smoking_habits = if_else(perc_smokers > 20, "Heavy Smokers", "Light Smokers")) |>
    mutate(obesity_distribution = if_else(obesity >37, "Higher Obesity Area", "Lower Obesity Area"))
  


join <- left_join(county_health, Poverty, by = c("County", "State"))
join <- distinct(join)
join <- join[join$County != "" & !is.na(join$County), ]

```

## Univariate Analyses
# Graph 1
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
univariate = function (variable, color = "chocolate"){
  variable_plot = ggplot(join)

variable_plot + geom_histogram(aes(x =variable), binwidth = 10, fill = color, col = "black") +   labs( x = paste(variable), y = "Count", title = "Distribution of", variable)
  
}

univariate(join$poor_health, "blue")

```
The distribution is skewed right. The median of percentage in poor health is 
`r median(join$poor_health)`
and the average is
`r round(mean(join$poor_health), digits = 2)`
.

## Multivariate Analyses
# Graph 1
Multivariate Analyses: Create at least 4 multivariate (2 or more variables) graphs to display the relationships among your variables of interest.  Provide a brief description of what your plots show, including one or more bivariate descriptive statistics.
```{r}
multivariate_num = function (x,y, color = "chocolate"){
  variable_plot = ggplot(join)

variable_plot + geom_point(aes(x =x, y = y), fill = color, col = "black") +   labs( x = paste(x), y = paste(y), title = paste(x, "vs.", y))
  
}
multivariate_num(join$perc_pov, join$low_birth)



```

The scatterplot has a right skewed distribution and the general trend is that the more prevelent poverty is in an area, the more likely it is that the county has a higher percentage of low weight at birth. When poverty is above the median, the percentage of babies born with a low birthweight is 
`r lightweight = join[join$perc_pov > 13.6,]
round (mean(lightweight$low_birth), digits = 2)`
and the average amount of poor mental health days for light smokers is 
`r heavyweight = join[join$perc_pov < 13.6,]
round (mean(heavyweight$low_birth), digits = 2)`
.

# Graph 2
```{r}
multivariate_num(join$perc_pov, join$poor_mental)

```
The scatterplot has a right skewed distribution and the general trend is that the more prevelent poverty is in an area, the more likely it is that the county has more residents with poor mental health. When poverty is above the median, the average percentage of residents with poor mental health is
`r poverty_mental = join[join$perc_pov > 13.6,]
round (mean(poverty_mental$poor_mental), digits = 2)`
and when poverty is below the median, the average percentage of residents with poor mental health is
`r less_pov = join[join$perc_pov < 13.6,]
round (mean(less_pov$poor_mental), digits = 2)`

## Choice elements
I used inline code in all of my descriptive statistics. I created two new variables by taking numerical variables such as percentage of obesity in counties and percentage of smokers in counties and I turned them into categorical variables by calculating the median and those that were higher than the median were either "higher obesity" or "higher smoking" areas. I also used a for loop and if statement to remove any na values from the first dataset. I joined two datasets together. For the univariate graphs, I created a function with 2 arguments, one argument being the variable and the second being the color of the graph.

## Conclusion

I found that living in poverty consistently contributed to poor health, both in physical health and mental health. Also, smoking led to poor mental health and obesity led to poor physical health. My conclusions were what I expected because a lack of financial stability can be bad for health, as well as obesity and smoking.

# Define server logic required to draw a histogram
server <- function(input, output) {
  filtered <- reactive({
    if (input$state == "USA") {
      health
    } else {
      subset(health, State == input$state)
    }
  })
  
  output$distPlot <- renderPlot({
    
    if(input$selectvar1 == 1 & input$selectvar2 == 5){
      hist(filtered()$low_birth, main='Distribution of Low Birth Weight',xlab='Percent of Low Weight Births',col = 'purple', border = 'darkgrey')
    }
    
    if(input$selectvar1 == 2 & input$selectvar2 == 5){
      hist(filtered()$poor_health, main='Distribution of Poor Health',xlab='Percent in Poor Health',col = 'purple', border = 'darkgrey')
      
    }
    if(input$selectvar1 == 3 & input$selectvar2 == 5){
      hist(filtered()$perc_pov, main='Distribution of Poverty',xlab='Percent in Poverty',col = 'purple', border = 'darkgrey')
      
    }
    if(input$selectvar1 == 4 & input$selectvar2 == 5){
      hist(filtered()$poor_mental, main='Distribution of Poor Mental Health',xlab='Amount of Poor Mental Health Days',col = 'purple', border = 'darkgrey')
      
    }
    
    if(input$selectvar1 == 1 & input$selectvar2 == 2){
      plot(filtered()$low_birth, filtered()$poor_health, xlab = "Percentage of Low Birth Weights", ylab = "Percentage of those in poor health", col = "chocolate")
      
    }
    if(input$selectvar1 == 1 & input$selectvar2 == 3){
      plot(filtered()$low_birth, filtered()$perc_pov, xlab = "Percentage of Low Birth Weights", ylab = "Percentage of those in poverty", col = "chocolate")
      
    }
    
    if(input$selectvar1 == 1 & input$selectvar2 == 4){
      plot(filtered()$low_birth, filtered()$poor_mental, xlab = "Percentage of Low Birth Weights", ylab = "Average amount of poor mental health days", col = "chocolate")
      
    }
    if(input$selectvar1 == 2 & input$selectvar2 == 1){
      plot(filtered()$poor_health, filtered()$low_birth, xlab = "Percentage of those in poor health", ylab = "Percentage of Low Birth Weights", col = "chocolate")
      
    }
    if(input$selectvar1 == 2 & input$selectvar2 == 3){
      plot(filtered()$poor_health, filtered()$perc_pov, xlab = "Percentage of those in poor health", ylab = "Percentage of those in poverty", col = "chocolate")
      
    }
    if(input$selectvar1 == 2 & input$selectvar2 == 4){
      plot(filtered()$poor_health, filtered()$poor_mental, xlab = "Percentage of those in poor health", ylab = "Average amount of poor mental health days", col = "chocolate")
      
    }
    
    if(input$selectvar1 == 3 & input$selectvar2 == 1){
      plot(filtered()$perc_pov, filtered()$low_birth, xlab = "Percentage of those in poverty", ylab = "Percentage of Low Birth Weights", col = "chocolate")
      
    }
    
    if(input$selectvar1 == 3 & input$selectvar2 == 2){
      plot(filtered()$perc_pov, filtered()$poor_health, xlab = "Percentage of those in poverty", ylab = "Percentage of those in poor health", col = "chocolate")
      
    }
    if(input$selectvar1 == 3 & input$selectvar2 == 4){
      plot(filtered()$perc_pov, filtered()$poor_mental, xlab = "Percentage of those in poverty", ylab = "Average amount of poor mental health days", col = "chocolate")
      
    }
    if(input$selectvar1 == 4 & input$selectvar2 == 1){
      plot(filtered()$poor_mental, filtered()$low_birth, xlab = "Average amount of poor mental health days", ylab = "Percentage of Low Birth Weights", col = "chocolate")
      
    }
    if(input$selectvar1 == 4 & input$selectvar2 == 2){
      plot(filtered()$poor_mental, filtered()$poor_health, xlab = "Average amount of poor mental health days", ylab = "Percentage of those in poor health", col = "chocolate")
      
    }
    if(input$selectvar1 == 4 & input$selectvar2 == 3){
      plot(filtered()$poor_mental, filtered()$perc_pov, xlab = "Average amount of poor mental health days", ylab = "Percentage of those in poverty", col = "chocolate")
      
    }
  })
  output$mean <- renderPrint({ 
    if(input$selectvar1 == 1 & input$selectvar2 == 5 & input$rounder == FALSE){
      mean(filtered()$low_birth, na.rm=TRUE)}
    else if(input$selectvar1 == 1 & input$selectvar2 == 5 & input$rounder == TRUE){
      round(mean(filtered()$low_birth, na.rm=TRUE), digits = 2)}
    
    else if(input$selectvar1 == 2 & input$selectvar2 == 5 &input$rounder == FALSE) {
      mean(filtered()$poor_health, na.rm=TRUE)}
    else if(input$selectvar1 == 2 & input$selectvar2 == 5 &input$rounder == TRUE) {

    else if(input$selectvar1 == 3 & input$selectvar2 == 5 & input$rounder == FALSE) {

    else if(input$selectvar1 == 4 & input$selectvar2 == 5 & input$rounder == FALSE) {
      sd(filtered()$poor_mental, na.rm=TRUE)}
    else if(input$selectvar1 == 4 & input$selectvar2 == 5 & input$rounder == TRUE) {
      round(sd(filtered()$poor_mental, na.rm=TRUE), digits = 2)}
    
  })
  output$cor <- renderPrint ({
    if(input$selectvar1 == 1 & input$selectvar2 == 2 & input$rounder == FALSE){
      cor(filtered()$low_birth,filtered()$poor_health)}
    else if(input$selectvar1 == 1 & input$selectvar2 == 2 & input$rounder == TRUE){
      round(cor(filtered()$low_birth,filtered()$poor_health), digits = 2)}
    
    else if(input$selectvar1 == 1 & input$selectvar2 == 3 &input$rounder == FALSE) {
      cor(filtered()$low_birth, filtered()$perc_pov)}
    else if(input$selectvar1 == 1 & input$selectvar2 == 3 &input$rounder == TRUE) {
      round(cor(filtered()$low_birth, filtered()$perc_pov), digits = 2)}
    
    else if(input$selectvar1 == 1 & input$selectvar2 == 4 & input$rounder == FALSE) {
      cor(filtered()$low_birth, filtered()$poor_mental)}
    else if(input$selectvar1 == 1 & input$selectvar2 == 4 & input$rounder == TRUE) {
      round(cor(filtered()$low_birth, filtered()$poor_mental), digits = 2)}
    
    else if(input$selectvar1 == 2 & input$selectvar2 == 1 & input$rounder == FALSE) {
      cor(filtered()$poor_health, filtered()$low_birth)}
    else if(input$selectvar1 == 2 & input$selectvar2 == 1 & input$rounder == TRUE) {
      round(cor(filtered()$poor_health, filtered()$low_birth), digits = 2)}
    
    else if(input$selectvar1 == 2 & input$selectvar2 == 3 & input$rounder == FALSE) {
      cor(filtered()$poor_health, filtered()$perc_pov)}
    else if(input$selectvar1 == 2 & input$selectvar2 == 3 & input$rounder == TRUE) {

      cor(filtered()$poor_health, filtered()$poor_mental)}
    else if(input$selectvar1 == 2 & input$selectvar2 == 4 & input$rounder == TRUE) {

}
